cards.text: At that time, Jesus is walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and His disciples are hungry. Friend, I know that kind of hungry. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer staring at a takeout menu for a place that closed down.

cards.question: In the grainfield on the Sabbath, the hungry disciples pick heads of grain and eat them.

cards.text: Then the Pharisees, a group of Jewish religious leaders, see what the disciples are doing. And they speak up right there in the field.

cards.question: The Pharisees see the disciples picking grain in the field. What do they tell Jesus about them?

answers.text: They're doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath
They're picking from somebody else's field
They're eating without washing their hands

cards.text: Jesus answers with a question: haven't they read what David, Israel's king, did when he and his companions were hungry? They bring Him a rulebook, and He hands them back a STORY.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Pharisees where David and his hungry companions went. Where was it?

cards.text: Inside the house of God, David and his companions eat the consecrated bread.

cards.question: Jesus says the consecrated bread in the house of God was lawful only for the ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus points to the Law: on the Sabbath, the priests in the temple break the Sabbath. That's ON the Sabbath, IN the temple, BY the priests, so read that one twice, friend.

cards.question: Jesus says the priests who break the Sabbath in the temple are guilty.
Right after talking about the priests in the temple, what does Jesus tell the Pharisees is here?

answers.text: A priest sent from the temple

cards.text: Then Jesus quotes the line "I desire mercy, not sacrifice" from the prophet Hosea (Hosea 6:6). Short line, heavy line.

cards.question: Jesus says if the Pharisees had known what 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice' means, they wouldn't have condemned the ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus finishes with a line about the Son of Man, a name He uses for Himself (Matthew 8:20). Friend, this is the line I'd hang right over my ovens.

cards.question: Jesus says the Son of Man is Lord of the ___.

cards.text: Jesus moves on from there and goes into their synagogue, where there's a man with a withered hand. Me, I couldn't move on from ANYWHERE for years, friend, because the back of a junk drawer has no exit.
Then they ask Jesus a question with that man RIGHT THERE in the room: "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?"

cards.question: In the synagogue, they ask Jesus if it's lawful to heal on the Sabbath in order to ___ Him.

cards.text: So that question is really a trap with a question mark glued on the end. Jesus answers with a sheep that falls into a pit on the Sabbath.

cards.question: Jesus asks about a sheep that falls into a pit on the Sabbath. What does He say its owner will do?

answers.text: Take hold of it and lift it out
Leave it there until the Sabbath ends
Ask a priest whether he can help

cards.question: Jesus says a man is much more ___ than a sheep.
In the synagogue, Jesus says it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to the man with the withered hand. They brought a question, friend, and Jesus is about to skip straight to the demonstration.

cards.question: What does Jesus tell the man with the withered hand?

answers.text: Go and wash in the Jordan
Go show yourself to the priest

cards.question: When the man stretches out his hand, it gets a little better but not all the way.
After the man's hand is restored, the Pharisees go out and plot how they might kill Jesus.

cards.text: Jesus is aware of what the Pharisees are plotting.

cards.question: Jesus knows the Pharisees are plotting to kill Him. What does He do?

answers.text: He goes back into their synagogue
He sends His disciples to them

cards.text: Large crowds follow Him. When I leave a room, friend, the only thing that follows me is my mustache.

cards.question: Jesus heals all of the people in the large crowds that follow Him.
Jesus has withdrawn and healed the crowds that follow Him. What does He warn them?

answers.text: Not to follow Him any farther
Not to go back to the synagogue

cards.text: The Gospel of Matthew says this was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 42:1-4): "Here is My Servant, whom I have chosen, My beloved, in whom My soul delights." The words go on: "I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will proclaim justice to the nations."

cards.question: In the words from Isaiah, the Servant will quarrel and cry out so everyone in the streets hears His voice.

cards.text: No quarreling, no voice in the streets. Then the words give two pictures: a bruised reed and a smoldering wick.

cards.question: What do the words from Isaiah say the Servant will do with a bruised reed and a smoldering wick?

answers.text: He will not break or extinguish them
He will gather and burn them
He will cut and replace them

cards.text: And Isaiah's words say that holds till He leads justice to victory.

cards.question: Isaiah's words end with the nations putting their ___ in the Servant's name.
